newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian army says 1984 riot deaths case closed.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian army says 1984 riot deaths case closed.

text.p: Indonesia's military said it will not reopen investigations into a 1984 riot in which troops killed at least 18 people, the official Antara news agency said on Sunday.
"That case is already finished and will not be reopened again," armed forces chief General Feisal Tanjung said during a military exercise on Indonesia's Natuna islands.

Last week there were calls to reopen the investigation after more than 200 people gathered at a local mosque to remember those people killed when troops fired on anti-government protesters in the Tanjung Priok port area of Jakarta.

The possibility of a new investigation had been left open after Defence Minister Edi Sudradjat was quoted as saying it would be some time before the government could attend to the request to reopen the investigation.
But Sudradjat was quoted by Antara as saying on Saturday that too much time had passed.
"It is too long since the incident so what can be investigated and looked for again. Besides that, it has to be asked what is the relevance as that incident is already over," he said.
The riots have never been independently investigated but the secretary-general of the National Commission on Human Rights, Baharuddin Lopa, had said the case would be discussed in December.
Tha Jakarta Post daily said the commission had received several requests for an investigation into the incident.
The government has said 18 people were killed in the riots, which erupted after Moslems battled police after inflammatory sermons were delivered in a mosque.
But human rights groups say the toll was at least 26 and some say the death toll could be as much as five times the official figure.

The national human rights commission, which was set up in 1993, has differed with the government version of riots in Jakarta in July this year, the worst disturbances in the capital in more than 20 years.
The government has said four people died but the commission has put the death toll at five and says at least 74 others had been reported missing.
